name: Approval prompt
summary: Asks the person before something that changes data happens: what will happen, the details that matter, a warning when it cannot be undone, and Cancel or the action itself.
use: just before an action that sends, pays, books or deletes, so the person confirms it first
a11y: A labelled section whose heading says what will happen; the details are a description list, and Cancel comes first in tab order so a stray Enter does not confirm.

use_when: an assistant is about to do something that changes data (send, pay, book, delete) and the person must say yes first
avoid_when: the action already happened: use receipt
the person still has to fill in values: use form-fields
a bill or request that goes through several approvers: use approval-panel

parts.name: title
parts.what: what will happen, as a question

parts.name: summary
parts.what: one line on what confirming does

parts.name: details
parts.what: one fact about the action: who, what, how much, when

parts.name: warning
parts.what: an optional caution, for actions that cannot be undone

parts.name: cancel
parts.what: the quiet way out, first in tab order

parts.name: approve
parts.what: the primary button that does the action

empty.how: with no details the details box is hidden, so only the question and the buttons show

loading.how: the prompt is shown only once the action is known; while it is being prepared show nothing

error.how: if the action fails after confirming, replace the prompt with error-retry

disabled.how: a disabled or still-loading button turns quiet neutral (secondary text on a subtle fill), still readable at AA

overflow.how: at most six details; on a phone each detail stacks label over value and the buttons share the row

long_text.how: titles, values and button labels wrap, also long addresses with no spaces

keyboard: Tab reaches Cancel first, then the action
Enter or Space presses the focused button
Escape cancels when the renderer shows it
